notes.heading: Overview
points: Welfare schemes are government initiatives aimed at improving socio-economic conditions of citizens
They focus on poverty alleviation, employment, health, education, and social security
These schemes implement Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)
They play a key role in inclusive and sustainable development

notes.heading: Meaning of Welfare Schemes
points: Welfare schemes are programs designed to support vulnerable and disadvantaged sections of society
They provide financial, social, and infrastructural support
They aim to reduce inequality and improve quality of life
They are implemented by central, state, or jointly by both governments
They are often targeted or universal in nature

notes.heading: Key Features of Welfare Schemes
points: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in many schemes
Use of Aadhaar and digital platforms for delivery
Convergence of multiple schemes for efficiency

notes.heading: Major Categories of Welfare Schemes
points: Social security schemes (e.g., pensions, insurance schemes)

notes.heading: Employment Welfare Schemes
points: MGNREGA provides 100 days of wage employment in rural areas
Promotes rural development and asset creation

notes.heading: Food Security Schemes
points: National Food Security Act ensures subsidized food grains
Public Distribution System (PDS) distributes essential commodities
Aims to reduce hunger and malnutrition
Covers large population under subsidized food supply

notes.heading: Health Welfare Schemes
points: Ayushman Bharat provides health insurance coverage

notes.heading: Housing Welfare Schemes
points: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) provides housing for all
Focus on rural and urban poor
Promotes dignity and improved living standards

notes.heading: Social Security Schemes
points: Pension schemes for elderly, widows, and disabled
Insurance schemes like PMJJBY and PMSBY
Focus on financial protection against risks
Encourages savings and security for poor households
Reduces vulnerability of informal sector workers

notes.heading: Importance of Welfare Schemes
points: Enhance quality of life of citizens

notes.heading: Challenges in Implementation
points: Leakages and corruption in delivery system

notes.heading: Role of Technology in Welfare Schemes
points: Mobile apps for monitoring and grievance redressal

name: Governance - Health: National Health Mission & National AYUSH Mission

notes.heading: Overview
points: Health sector schemes aim to improve accessibility, affordability, and quality of healthcare in India
National Health Mission (NHM) is the umbrella program for strengthening public health systems
National AYUSH Mission (NAM) promotes traditional systems of medicine
Both focus on universal health coverage and holistic healthcare

notes.heading: National Health Mission (NHM) - Introduction
points: Launched in 2013 by merging National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and National Urban Health Mission (NUHM)
Aims to provide accessible, affordable, and quality healthcare services
Focuses on strengthening public health infrastructure
Covers both rural and urban populations
Emphasizes preventive, promotive, and curative healthcare

notes.heading: Objectives of NHM
points: Reduce maternal and infant mortality rates
Provide universal access to equitable healthcare
Promote health awareness and preventive care

notes.heading: Key Components of NHM
points: Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCH+A)

notes.heading: Important Features of NHM
points: ASHA workers for community-level health support
Integration of health services at all levels
Use of digital health initiatives and monitoring systems

notes.heading: Importance of NHM
points: Improves health indicators like IMR and MMR
Reduces burden on secondary and tertiary hospitals

notes.heading: Challenges of NHM
points: Shortage of medical professionals in rural areas

notes.heading: National AYUSH Mission (NAM) - Introduction
points: Launched in 2014 to promote traditional Indian systems of medicine
AYUSH stands for Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy
Focus on integration of AYUSH with mainstream healthcare
Promotes holistic and preventive healthcare approach
Encourages use of traditional knowledge systems

notes.heading: Objectives of National AYUSH Mission
points: Promote AYUSH medical systems across India
Improve availability of AYUSH healthcare services
Integrate AYUSH with National Health Mission
Ensure quality control of AYUSH drugs

notes.heading: Key Features of AYUSH Mission
points: Establishment of AYUSH hospitals and dispensaries
Support for cultivation of medicinal plants
Promotion of AYUSH education and research
Integration with public health delivery system
Standardization and quality control of medicines

notes.heading: Importance of AYUSH Mission
points: Increases accessibility in rural and remote areas
Reduces burden on allopathic healthcare system

notes.heading: Challenges of AYUSH Mission
points: Lack of scientific validation in some treatments

notes.heading: Comparison of NHM and AYUSH Mission
points: NHM focuses on modern public healthcare system
AYUSH focuses on traditional medicine systems
AYUSH emphasizes holistic and preventive care
Both aim at Universal Health Coverage in India

notes.heading: Overall Significance in Governance
points: Combines modern and traditional medicine approaches
Supports Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being)

name: Governance - Jan Aushadhi Scheme, Mission Indradhanush & NFHS-4

notes.heading: Overview
points: These initiatives are key components of India’s public health and welfare system
They focus on affordable medicines, immunization, and health data collection
They aim to improve accessibility, affordability, and evidence-based policymaking

notes.heading: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) / Jan Aushadhi Scheme
points: Launched to provide quality generic medicines at affordable prices
Jan Aushadhi Kendras sell medicines at much lower cost than branded drugs
Implemented by Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India (BPPI)
Focus on reducing out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare
Promotes use of generic medicines in India

notes.heading: Key Features of Jan Aushadhi Scheme
points: Availability of generic medicines at low cost
Wide network of Jan Aushadhi stores across India
Medicines tested for quality and efficacy
Focus on essential drugs for common diseases

notes.heading: Importance of Jan Aushadhi Scheme
points: Reduces financial burden on poor households

notes.heading: Challenges of Jan Aushadhi Scheme
points: Perception of lower quality despite certification
Uneven spread of stores across regions

notes.heading: Mission Indradhanush
points: Launched in 2014 to increase full immunization coverage of children
Targets children and pregnant women who are unvaccinated or partially vaccinated
Focus on diseases like diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, polio, tuberculosis, measles
Aims to achieve full immunization coverage across India

notes.heading: Key Features of Mission Indradhanush
points: Focus on high-risk and underserved areas
Use of data-driven identification of beneficiaries
Special attention to remote and urban slum areas

notes.heading: Importance of Mission Indradhanush
points: Supports Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being)

notes.heading: National Family Health Survey-4 (NFHS-4)
points: Conducted in 2015-16 by International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS)
Provides data on population, health, and nutrition indicators
Covers fertility, mortality, family planning, maternal and child health
Includes data on nutrition and anemia
Provides state and national level health indicators

notes.heading: Key Findings of NFHS-4
points: Decline in Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in most states
High prevalence of anemia among women and children

notes.heading: Importance of NFHS-4
points: Provides evidence base for health policy formulation

notes.heading: Challenges in NFHS Data Utilization
points: Need for real-time health data systems
Limited use of data at local governance level

notes.heading: Overall Significance in Governance
points: Strengthens preventive and curative healthcare system
Improves maternal and child health outcomes
Enhances public health governance in India

name: Governance - Education Schemes (Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat, Mid Day Meal, GIAN, SWAYAM)

notes.heading: Overview
points: Education schemes aim to improve access, equity, quality, and inclusiveness in India’s education system
They target foundational learning, school nutrition, higher education, and digital learning
Government focuses on reducing dropout rates and improving learning outcomes

notes.heading: Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB)
points: Launched in 2014 as a sub-program under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
Focuses on foundational learning of reading, writing, and mathematics
Targets students of Classes I and II
Emphasizes early grade literacy and numeracy (EGLN)
Encourages joyful learning environment in primary education

notes.heading: Key Features of PBBB
points: Improvement in reading and writing skills at early stage
Use of learning materials like storybooks and worksheets

notes.heading: Importance of PBBB
points: Builds strong foundation for future education
Reduces learning gaps at early stage

notes.heading: Mid Day Meal Scheme (MDM)
points: Launched in 1995 as a centrally sponsored scheme
Provides free lunch to children in government and government-aided schools
Targets students of Classes I to VIII
Aims to improve nutrition and school attendance
Largest school feeding program in the world

notes.heading: Key Features of Mid Day Meal Scheme
points: Hot cooked meals provided in schools
Joint responsibility of central and state governments

notes.heading: Importance of Mid Day Meal Scheme
Challenges of Mid Day Meal Scheme
points: Quality and hygiene issues in some regions
Leakages and corruption in supply chain

notes.heading: GIAN (Global Initiative of Academic Networks)
points: Launched in 2015 under Ministry of Education
Aims to attract global academicians and scientists to Indian institutions
Focus on knowledge sharing and innovation

notes.heading: Key Features of GIAN
points: Foreign experts teach short-term courses in Indian institutions
Encourages interaction between Indian and global faculty
Focus on advanced research and innovation

notes.heading: Importance of GIAN
points: Improves quality of higher education in India
Brings global expertise to Indian classrooms

notes.heading: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds)
points: Launched to provide online education platform in India
Covers school, undergraduate, postgraduate, and skill courses
Developed by Government of India in collaboration with IITs and IGNOU
Aims to bridge digital divide in education

notes.heading: Key Features of SWAYAM
points: Free access to high-quality online courses
Video lectures, reading material, and assessments

notes.heading: Importance of SWAYAM
points: Promotes digital learning and education accessibility

notes.heading: Overall Significance in Governance
points: Strengthens foundational and higher education systems

name: Governance - Health & Tribal Welfare Schemes (JSY, JSSK, SC/ST, Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana)

notes.heading: Overview
points: These schemes focus on maternal health, child health, and welfare of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST)
They aim to reduce maternal and infant mortality and promote inclusive development
Government emphasizes equity in health services and tribal upliftment

notes.heading: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
points: Launched in 2005 under National Health Mission
Aims to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality
Promotes institutional delivery among pregnant women
Combines cash assistance with antenatal and postnatal care
Targets poor pregnant women especially in low-performing states

notes.heading: Key Features of JSY
points: Focus on Below Poverty Line (BPL) women
Antenatal care and safe delivery promotion

notes.heading: Importance of JSY
points: Improves maternal and child health outcomes

notes.heading: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
points: Launched in 2011 under National Health Mission
Aims to eliminate out-of-pocket expenses for pregnant women and sick infants
Provides free maternal and child healthcare services
Focus on institutional delivery and neonatal care
Ensures universal access to healthcare services

notes.heading: Key Features of JSSK
points: Free delivery (normal and caesarean) in public hospitals
Free drugs, diagnostics, and diet during hospitalization
Free transport from home to facility and back
Free treatment for sick infants up to 1 year
24x7 availability of services in public health facilities

notes.heading: Importance of JSSK
points: Reduces financial burden on poor families

notes.heading: Scheduled Castes (SC)
points: SCs are historically disadvantaged communities listed under Article 341 of the Constitution
They face social, educational, and economic backwardness
Government provides affirmative action and reservation benefits
Focus on social justice and equality

notes.heading: Scheduled Tribes (ST)
points: STs are indigenous communities listed under Article 342
They have distinct culture, language, and geographical isolation
Face issues of marginalization and lack of development
Government provides special protection and welfare schemes
Focus on preserving tribal identity and development

notes.heading: Key Features of SC/ST Welfare
points: Legal protection under SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act

notes.heading: Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana (VKY)
points: Launched for holistic development of tribal communities
Implemented by Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Focus on convergence of existing schemes for tribal welfare
Aims at improving quality of life in tribal areas
Targets infrastructure, education, health, and livelihood

notes.heading: Key Features of VKY
points: Improvement in education and healthcare facilities

notes.heading: Importance of VKY
points: Improves human development indicators in tribal areas
Preserves tribal culture while promoting modernization

notes.heading: Overall Significance in Governance
points: Improves maternal and child health outcomes
Promotes tribal and marginalized community welfare

name: Governance - Inclusion, Disability & Rural-Urban Development (PMAGY, Disability, Accessible India Campaign)

notes.heading: Overview
points: These initiatives focus on inclusive development of marginalized communities, especially SC villages, persons with disabilities, and rural-urban infrastructure
They aim to reduce social exclusion and improve access to basic services
Government emphasis is on equitable development and barrier-free society

notes.heading: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY)

Aims at integrated development of SC-dominated villages
Focus on basic infrastructure and social development indicators
Encourages convergence of existing government schemes
Targets reduction of poverty and social disparities in SC villages

notes.heading: Key Features of PMAGY

Provision of roads, housing, sanitation, drinking water, and electricity
Improvement in education and health facilities
Village development planning with community participation

notes.heading: Importance of PMAGY

Implemented by Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
Supports inclusive and universal design principles

notes.heading: Key Features of Accessible India Campaign
Importance of Accessible India Campaign

name: Governance - Rural Development Missions (SAGY, Rurban Mission, DDUGJY, Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday)

notes.heading: Overview
points: These initiatives focus on holistic rural development through infrastructure, governance, energy access, and model village development
They aim to bridge rural-urban divide and improve quality of life in villages
Government emphasizes convergence of schemes, participatory governance, and sustainable rural growth

notes.heading: Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)
points: Launched in 2014 to develop model villages through Members of Parliament (MPs)
Focus on holistic development of selected Gram Panchayats
Aims at social, cultural, and infrastructure transformation of villages
Encourages community participation and local governance
Does not provide separate funds; uses convergence of existing schemes

notes.heading: Key Features of SAGY
points: Each MP adopts villages for development
Focus on sanitation, education, health, and livelihood
Emphasis on social harmony and behavioral change

notes.heading: Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan
points: Launched in 2016 to strengthen Panchayati Raj system
Coincides with National Panchayati Raj Day celebrations
Aims to promote social harmony and rural development

notes.heading: Key Features of Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan

Focus on social inclusion and harmony

Challenges of Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan

Focus on providing infrastructure and economic development in rural areas

notes.heading: Key Features of SPMRM
points: Provision of urban-like facilities in rural areas
Focus on skill development and economic activities

notes.heading: Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
points: Launched in 2014 to improve rural electrification
Focus on feeder separation for agricultural and non-agricultural use
Strengthens power infrastructure in rural areas

notes.heading: Key Features of DDUGJY

Strengthening of sub-transmission and distribution networks
Improvement of power reliability in rural areas
Focus on energy efficiency and infrastructure

notes.heading: Challenges of DDUGJY

name: Governance - Rural & Urban Infrastructure Schemes (PMGSY, Swachh Bharat, PMAY-G, PMAY-U)

notes.heading: Overview
points: These schemes focus on improving basic infrastructure in rural and urban India
They aim at housing, sanitation, connectivity, and quality of life improvements
Government emphasizes inclusive and sustainable infrastructure development

notes.heading: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)
points: Launched in 2000 to provide all-weather road connectivity to rural habitations
Aims to connect unconnected villages with population thresholds
Improves access to markets, education, and healthcare
Implemented by Ministry of Rural Development
Uses GIS and quality monitoring systems for implementation

notes.heading: Key Features of PMGSY
points: Focus on habitations without road access
Use of standardized road construction norms
Funding shared between Centre and States

notes.heading: Importance of PMGSY
points: Improves access to services and markets

notes.heading: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (SBA)
points: Launched in 2014 to achieve universal sanitation coverage
Aims to eliminate open defecation in India
Focus on behavioral change and sanitation infrastructure
Implemented by Ministry of Jal Shakti and Urban Affairs

notes.heading: Key Features of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan
Importance of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan

notes.heading: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G)
points: Launched in 2016 to provide pucca houses to rural poor
Aims to achieve Housing for All in rural areas
Provides financial assistance for house construction
Beneficiary identification through Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC)

notes.heading: Key Features of PMAY-G
points: Minimum house size and quality standards
Focus on women ownership of houses

notes.heading: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U)
points: Launched in 2015 to provide housing for urban poor
Aims at Housing for All in urban areas
Focus on slum redevelopment and affordable housing
Implemented by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

notes.heading: Overall Significance in Governance
points: Improves basic infrastructure and quality of life

name: Governance - Urban Development Missions (Housing for All, Smart Cities, HRIDAY, AMRUT)

notes.heading: Overview
points: These initiatives focus on planned urbanization, housing, heritage conservation, and urban infrastructure development
They aim to improve quality of life in cities and ensure sustainable urban growth
Government emphasis is on inclusive, technology-driven, and citizen-centric urban governance

notes.heading: Housing for All by 2022 (PMAY)
points: A national mission aimed at providing affordable housing to all eligible urban and rural households
Implemented through PMAY-Urban and PMAY-Gramin components
Focus on economically weaker sections (EWS), low-income groups (LIG), and middle-income groups (MIG)
Encourages public-private partnerships and credit-linked subsidies
Targets elimination of housing shortage in India

notes.heading: Key Features of Housing for All
points: Focus on women ownership and inclusive housing

notes.heading: Challenges of Housing for All
points: High construction costs in urban areas

notes.heading: Smart Cities Mission
points: Launched in 2015 to develop 100 smart cities across India
Aims to promote sustainable and citizen-friendly urban development
Focus on technology-driven governance and infrastructure
Encourages area-based development and pan-city solutions
Implemented by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

notes.heading: Key Features of Smart Cities Mission
points: Smart governance using ICT and e-governance

notes.heading: Importance of Smart Cities Mission
points: Enhances quality of life in cities

notes.heading: Challenges of Smart Cities Mission
points: Digital divide in access to services

notes.heading: HRIDAY (National Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana)
points: Launched in 2015 to preserve and revitalize heritage cities
Focus on holistic development of heritage urban areas
Combines heritage conservation with infrastructure development
Implemented by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Selected heritage cities across India are covered

notes.heading: Key Features of HRIDAY
points: Improvement of basic infrastructure in heritage areas
Preservation of cultural and historical identity
Development of pilgrimage and tourism infrastructure
Integrated urban planning for heritage cities

notes.heading: Importance of HRIDAY
points: Improves urban infrastructure in heritage cities

notes.heading: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)
points: Launched in 2015 to provide basic urban infrastructure
Focus on water supply, sewerage, drainage, and urban transport
Aims to improve quality of life in urban areas
Implemented by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

notes.heading: Challenges of AMRUT
